module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 433

*References:*
- [Erdős Problem 433](https://www.erdosproblems.com/433)
- P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *On a linear Diophantine problem of Frobenius*,
  Acta Arithmetica 21 (1972), 399–408.
- J. Dixmier, *Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham on Frobenius' coin problem*,
  Proceedings of the AMS 109 (1990), 567–577.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos433

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- The Frobenius number of a finite set $A$: the greatest natural number outside the
additive submonoid generated by $A$. -/
noncomputable def frobeniusNumber (A : Finset ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m | m ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure (A : Set ℕ)}

/-- The largest Frobenius number of a $k$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose
elements have greatest common divisor one. -/
noncomputable def g (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ A.card = k ∧ A.gcd id = 1 ∧
    m = frobeniusNumber A}

/-- For every fixed $k \geq 2$, Erdős and Graham conjectured that
$$g(k,n) \sim \frac{n^2}{k-1}.$$
The conjecture was proved by Dixmier [Di90]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_433 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k, 2 ≤ k →
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (g k n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 / ((k : ℝ) - 1))) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos433

findings.description: The module bibliography places Dixmier’s proof in Proceedings of the AMS 109 (1990), 567–577. The cited result is actually in Journal of Number Theory 34(2) (1990), 198–209, with the title “Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham concerning the problem of Frobenius.” This is a reference error, not a defect in the mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The references at https://erdosproblems.com/latex/433 identify [Di90] as Dixmier, “Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham concerning the problem of Frobenius,” J. Number Theory (1990), 198–209. Crossref’s record for DOI 10.1016/0022-314X(90)90150-P confirms volume 34, issue 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the Dixmier reference with: J. Dixmier, Proof of a conjecture by Erdős and Graham concerning the problem of Frobenius, Journal of Number Theory 34(2) (1990), 198–209, DOI 10.1016/0022-314X(90)90150-P.

reformulations.difference: The helper uses a natural-valued supremum. For an admissible set containing 1 it returns 0, whereas the source’s greatest unrepresentable integer is −1. This convention does not change the file’s asymptotic theorem.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For gcd-one sets not containing 1, the helper equals the genuine Frobenius number; this follows from Mathlib’s FrobeniusNumber characterization and was checked in Lean. For every k ≥ 2 and n ≥ k+1, {2,…,k+1} is admissible and has a positive Frobenius number. Thus sets containing 1 cannot maximize either convention. The integer-valued source maximum consequently equals the cast of Lean’s g throughout this tail. Earlier values, including empty admissible families, do not affect the limit. /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves this eventual equality and the resulting ↔ between the two limit statements; its proofs do not depend on sorryAx.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The source explicitly identifies the fixed-k, n→∞ regime, matching the quantifiers, and its affirmative solution matches answer(True) and research solved. Lean checks establish finite-max semantics for g, the relevant Frobenius-number characterization, boundary values including g 2 2 = 0 and g 2 3 = 1, and equivalence of the ratio limit with asymptotic equivalence. The consolidated checks compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Dixmier’s full text could not be retrieved; the problem’s complete LaTeX source and Crossref supplied the statement/status and bibliographic information needed for this review.
